scope: Both surviving neo-Gothic coral-limestone Parliament wings on their complete separate native footprints, low roofs/parapets/rounded ends, physically open upper pointed-arch galleries and lower arcades, courtyard-facing gabled entrances, projecting shuttered oriels, west-wing clock tower/battlements/pinnacles and intrinsic green courtyard/front railings. Courtyard remains open; eastern lost/sunken tower, interiors, Treasury/RBC/other neighbors, roads, fountain, plants, people and vehicles excluded.

quallaSearch.notes: Started/finished with four existing published QuallaPD-selfdaylight originals. Night/event/fountain, unrelated and attribution/share-alike images were not needed. No supplemental imagery.

references.caption: Parliament building (west wing) in Bridgetown, Barbados Housing the Parliament Museum[1] and cafeteria

originalReview.notes: Four exact published native QuallaPD-selforiginals inspected. Regani2272x1704west-wing view shows pale/grey coursed coral stone, rounded south end, tall pale green projecting shuttered oriels with sloped red-brown hoods/brackets, small pointed lights, stepped battering buttress feet, open pointed gallery, corbelled cornice and four-faced black/gold clock on the square battlement/pinnacle tower. Two640x480CaribDigitaeast-wing views show long open upper pointed arcade/green balustrade, lower round arcade, projecting courtyard-facing pointed/gabled entrance block, low hipped roofs and rounded far end. KevinGabbert2000x1500published photograph shows matching green iron front rails/gates and west gallery/gabled entry/tower; tree obstruction/hidden detail is not copied. Original native footprints retain both separate wings and actual rounded/faceted ends; no native roof heights or separate tower polygon exists, so roof sections/tower placement within the west projection and small concealed details are bounded estimates. No supplemental imagery or photo texture used.
